thread_pair_example: driver input: 4 tokens (blocks), E = 256 experts, K = 8: 8 warps, after the first per-warp top-K there are 8*8 = 64 candidates > 32, so the stage loop runs once with stage_warps = 2. Warp 0 (threads 0..31) reads sh_key/sh_payload/sh_idx[0..31] at L277-279 and warp 1 (threads 32..63) reads [32..63]; then lane k of warp 1 (thread 32+k) writes sh_*[1*8+k] = sh_*[8+k] at L290-292, which lies inside warp 0's read window [0..31]. E.g. block 0: thread 8 (warp 0, lane 8) reads sh_key[8] (L277) vs thread 32 (warp 1, lane 0) writes sh_key[1*8+0] = sh_key[8] (L290, k = 0); likewise sh_payload[8..15] (L278/L291) and sh_idx[8..15] (L279/L292). Between the reads and the writes of a stage there is no barrier (the only barrier of the stage is L298, after the whole if-block). Needs num_warps*K > 32.
class_reason: All accesses are plain 32-bit shared-memory loads and stores (plain LDS / STS on dynamic shared arrays, no volatile, no atomics, no .STRONG token) by threads of different warps with no barrier between warp 0's reads of its 32-wide window and warp 1's K-wide write slice that overlaps it: plain-vs-plain unordered conflict, hence data race (DR) under D20; no strong access, so not SC.
buggy_expected: DR, cross-warp shared WAR on sh_key, sh_payload and sh_idx of routing_ds3_nogroup_topk_kernel (L277-279 loads vs L290-292 stores); the two other kernels of the file are reported in the same way for their own pairs (additional_pairs)

fixed.reason: the fix hoists the three loads out of the `if (warp_id < stage_warps)` block to the top of the stage (fixed L277-L280: pos = t; key/payload/idx loaded into registers by every thread) and adds __syncthreads() (fixed L281) before any warp enters the K-iteration write phase (fixed L294-296 for the stores), so every read of the stage happens before every write of the stage; the barrier at the end of the stage (fixed L302) orders the writes before the next stage's loads. verify.expected_report_fixed: nothing for those pairs.

routing_std_kernel L634 `max_red[warp_id] = max_logit;` is executed by all 32 lanes of a warp with the same value (intra-warp same-address same-value stores, present in both variants); not part of the target pair, a detector might still flag it.
Manifestation of these races is timing dependent (a fast warp must overtake a slow one); the sm_75 smoke run shows correct top-K for both variants; detection is by happens-before.

Primary pair confirmed at 0c4804c: E = 256 -> num_warps = 8, K = 8 -> 64 candidates > 32, one stage with stage_warps = 2 (routing.cu:269-272); warps 0 and 1 load sh_key/sh_payload/sh_idx[t] (L276-279) and lane k of warp w stores sh_*[w*8 + k] (L288-292) with no barrier until L298; warp 1's slice [8..15] lies in warp 0's read window, so thread 8 + k (warp 0) vs thread 32 + k (warp 1): 32-bit plain/plain WAR -> DR.
